title: jk.toml
description: JumpKick project manifest. Top-level identity and language keys, the core tables, and the dependency scopes. Plugin-owned tables ([micronaut], [android], ...) are allowed and documented by their plugins.

name.description: Module identity; never inherited from the workspace.

group.description: Maven groupId, or { workspace = true } in a member.

version.description: Version string, or { workspace = true } in a member.

sources.description: Sources jar: true → assembled by jk publish only; "always" → built by jk package. A library (no [application]) builds it regardless.

javadoc.description: Javadoc jar for a library: false → not built; "strict" → javadoc's doclint checks fail the step; default lenient (-Xdoclint:none, warnings in the results).

repositories.description: [repositories] table: one entry per remote, keyed by the name jk-lock.toml records as the source. An entry is a URL string or a table.

url.description: Base URL: https://, s3://, gs://, or file://. Plaintext http:// needs allow-insecure.

token.description: Bearer token; ${VAR} expands when the repository is used.

username.description: Basic-auth user; ${VAR} expands when the repository is used.

password.description: Basic-auth password; ${VAR} expands when the repository is used.

access-key.description: Object-store access key; ${VAR} expands when the repository is used.

secret-key.description: Object-store secret key; ${VAR} expands when the repository is used.

session-token.description: Object-store session token; ${VAR} expands when the repository is used.

groups.description: Exclusive Maven groups: exact or prefix.* patterns that resolve only from this repository.

allow-insecure.description: Accept a plaintext http:// URL for this repository. Refused on central.

blocked.description: The repository is asked of nothing and named when a package resolves nowhere, as Maven 3.9 blocks a plaintext http repository; written by jk import for a POM-declared http URL. Not beside allow-insecure.

allow-unverified.description: Pin an artifact this repository publishes no .sha256/.sha1 sidecar for; the lock summary counts them. Refused on central.

releases.description: Ask this repository for release versions (default true). false makes it snapshot-only.

snapshots.description: Ask this repository for -SNAPSHOT versions (default true). false makes it releases-only.

profiles.description: [profiles] table; keys are documented in docs/user.

features.description: [features] table; keys are documented in docs/user.

workspace.description: [workspace] table; keys are documented in docs/user.

manifest.description: [manifest] table; keys are documented in docs/user.

plugins.description: [plugins] table; keys are documented in docs/user.

relocate.description: Package relocation in the fat jar: source package prefix to shaded package prefix.

library.description: [library] table: what a library ships beyond its thin jar. A module declares [library] or [application], never both.

assembly.description: Package a fat (assembly) jar beside the thin jar.

relocate.description: Package relocation in the fat jar: source package prefix to shaded package prefix. Implies assembly; workspace siblings compile and run against the relocating -all.jar.

native.description: [native] table; keys are documented in docs/user.

image.description: [image] table; keys are documented in docs/user.

train.description: [train] table; keys are documented in docs/user.

build.description: [build] table: how this module compiles and tests. Keys are documented in docs/user/build.md.

order-after.description: Modules this one builds after, without a classpath edge.

test-plugin-jars.description: Plugin jars placed on the test worker's classpath.

debug.description: Debug information javac writes: full (-g: source, lines, local variables; the default, as Gradle and Maven compile), lines (-g:source,lines) or none (-g:none). A compile input.

ksp-options.description: KSP processor options as key=value strings.

extra-src.description: Extra module-relative source roots compiled with the main sources.

test-workers.description: Test JVMs for this module: 0 = the build's auto share, 1 = serial.

test-parallel.description: false is the same as test-workers = 1.

test.description: [test] table; keys are documented in docs/user.

assertions.description: Run every forked test JVM with -ea, as Surefire and Gradle do. Default true; false runs the suite with Java and Kotlin assert statements disabled. A run-tests input: flipping it re-runs the suite.

jvm-args.description: Flags appended verbatim to every forked test JVM after jk's own tuning (-Xmx, -Xss, --add-opens, an agent); Surefire's <argLine>. A run-tests input.

system-properties.description: One -Dkey=value per entry on every forked test JVM, a number or boolean rendered as its string; Surefire's <systemPropertyVariables>. A run-tests input.

dev.description: [dev] table: what `jk dev` runs beside the application, and how it tells the application itself is listening. Read by no other verb; never part of an action key.

sidecars.description: One table per sidecar, keyed by name, started in this order.

command.description: A string split like a shell would (quotes group; a backslash is literal unless it precedes a quote, a space, or a backslash; no expansion, no shell) or an argv array.

cwd.description: Working directory, relative to the manifest that declares the sidecar. Default "." (the manifest's own directory).

env.description: Values laid over the inherited environment and the .env files. Default: none.

ready.description: HTTP(S) URL polled every 250 ms (HTTP/1.1) until it answers 2xx/3xx; `localhost` is tried on both loopbacks. Default: no URL probe — with neither `ready` nor `ready-pattern`, one second alive is ready.

ready-pattern.description: Regex matched against the sidecar's stdout and stderr lines; the alternative to `ready`. Default: none.

ready-timeout.description: How long a probe may take: "60s", "2m", "500ms", or a bare number of seconds. A probe that times out fails the `jk dev` session. Default "60s".

front-door.description: Print this sidecar's `ready` URL in the one `ready ·` line once the whole session is ready. Default false.

restart.description: What to do when the sidecar exits on its own: `never` reports the exit once and the session continues; `on-exit` restarts with backoff, up to five failures in a row. Default "never".

ready.description: The application's own probe: an HTTP(S) URL polled every 250 ms (HTTP/1.1) after each start and restart until it answers 2xx/3xx; `localhost` is tried on both loopbacks. `dev-ready` and the `ready ·` line wait for it. Default: no probe — the app counts as ready once forked.

ready-pattern.description: Regex matched against the application's stdout and stderr lines; the alternative to `ready`. On a terminal this pipes the app's output through jk so it can be read. Default: none.

ready-timeout.description: How long the application's probe may take: "60s", "2m", "500ms", or a bare number of seconds. A probe that times out fails the `jk dev` session, as a sidecar's does. Default "60s".

format.description: [format] table; keys are documented in docs/user.

resolve.description: [resolve] table; keys are documented in docs/user.

variants.description: [variants] table; keys are documented in docs/user.

jvm.description: [jvm] table; keys are documented in docs/user.

deny.description: [deny] table; keys are documented in docs/user.

env.description: [env] table: what this module's workers (the compiler, each test JVM, plugin steps) may take from the environment beyond jk's allow-list. Per module; not inherited from a workspace root. Not an action-key input by itself.

inherit.description: true hands the module's workers the engine's whole environment, secrets included. Default false. Write the reason beside it.

vars.description: The [test] env shape: a bare name forwards the caller's value when it is set; a table sets values outright (${VAR}, ${module} and ${target} expand; an unset ${VAR} is an error). Reaches every worker of the module; [test] env layers on top for test JVMs.

audit.description: [audit] table: what `jk audit` reports without gating on. Read by the audit alone; never part of an action key.

ignore.description: Advisories the audit reports as ignored and leaves out of the exit status, in this order (the first entry naming an advisory wins).

id.description: The advisory id as the audit reports it (GHSA-…, CVE-…).

reason.description: Why the finding is accepted. Required; an entry without one is refused.

until.description: Last day the entry ignores (ISO YYYY-MM-DD). From the day after, the finding gates again and is reported as `ignore expired`.

guards.description: [guards] table: on-build (default true) moves the module and workspace guard lanes to --guard when false; coverage-report names the coverage XML the coverage.* measures read. Rules live in jk-guards.toml.

config.description: [config] table; keys are documented in docs/user.

forge.description: [forge] table; keys are documented in docs/user.

kotlin-plugins.description: [kotlin-plugins] table; keys are documented in docs/user.

javac.description: [javac] table: the javac plugins compile-main and compile-test invoke, and verbatim javac args. A compile input — part of the compile action key.

plugins.description: One table per plugin, keyed by the plugin's registered javac name (case-sensitive; passed as -Xplugin:<name>). The jar is a [processor-dependencies] entry.

options.description: Options handed to the plugin after its name.

args.description: Verbatim javac arguments, appended after every plugin.

test.description: [javac.test]: the same two keys, plus `release`; when present this table replaces [javac] for compile-test (an empty table turns the plugins off for the suite).

release.description: The `--release` compile-test targets, when the suite is to use a newer API than the module's `java` level: a java = 17 library tested with JDK 21 test code. Not below `java`; compile-main and the published class-file level are untouched. Default: the module's `java`.

m2.description: [m2] table; keys are documented in docs/user.

install.description: [install] table; keys are documented in docs/user.

dokka.description: [dokka]: how a Kotlin or mixed module's javadoc jar is documented (docs/user/packaging.md). A pure Java module never reads it.

version.description: The Dokka release: a bare version pins, ^2 floats within the line, latest is the newest stable. Default "2.2.0".

format.description: What Dokka writes into the jar: "javadoc" (default), the javadoc-shaped output Central's javadoc jar convention expects, or Dokka's own "html".

build-info.description: [build-info]: the jar carries git.properties (git.commit.id, git.commit.id.abbrev, git.branch, git.commit.time, git.dirty, git.build.time, git.build.version, git.closest.tag.name) and, for a Spring Boot application, META-INF/build-info.properties. An empty table is the battery at its defaults (docs/user/packaging.md).

file.description: Resource path of the git properties file inside the jar. Default "git.properties".

time.description: What git.build.time and build.time record: "commit" (default) is the HEAD commit's time, so one commit's builds are byte-identical; "build" is the wall clock, so every build regenerates the file and repackages the jar.

publish.description: [publish]: the POM metadata a release carries (docs/user/publish.md). A workspace root's table applies to every member that declares none. Maven Central requires all of them.

export-dependencies.description: [export-dependencies]: one dependency per key — a version string when the key is a catalog short name, a group:artifact[:version] string (versionless = platform-managed), "managed" on a catalog short name a platform BOM covers, or { group, name, version, features, ... }. A bare version is an exact pin; ^ ~ ranges and latest are opt-in.

dependencies.description: [dependencies]: one dependency per key — a version string when the key is a catalog short name, a group:artifact[:version] string (versionless = platform-managed), "managed" on a catalog short name a platform BOM covers, or { group, name, version, features, ... }. A bare version is an exact pin; ^ ~ ranges and latest are opt-in.

provided-dependencies.description: [provided-dependencies]: one dependency per key — a version string when the key is a catalog short name, a group:artifact[:version] string (versionless = platform-managed), "managed" on a catalog short name a platform BOM covers, or { group, name, version, features, ... }. A bare version is an exact pin; ^ ~ ranges and latest are opt-in.

runtime-dependencies.description: [runtime-dependencies]: one dependency per key — a version string when the key is a catalog short name, a group:artifact[:version] string (versionless = platform-managed), "managed" on a catalog short name a platform BOM covers, or { group, name, version, features, ... }. A bare version is an exact pin; ^ ~ ranges and latest are opt-in.

test-dependencies.description: [test-dependencies]: one dependency per key — a version string when the key is a catalog short name, a group:artifact[:version] string (versionless = platform-managed), "managed" on a catalog short name a platform BOM covers, or { group, name, version, features, ... }. A bare version is an exact pin; ^ ~ ranges and latest are opt-in.

plugin-dependencies.description: [plugin-dependencies]: refused — jk lock writes a pinned third-party plugin's SDK floor (jk-plugin-sdk, jk-host) into jk-lock.toml under the plugin scope itself; declare the plugin under [plugins].

processor-dependencies.description: [processor-dependencies]: one dependency per key — a version string when the key is a catalog short name, a group:artifact[:version] string (versionless = platform-managed), "managed" on a catalog short name a platform BOM covers, or { group, name, version, features, ... }. A bare version is an exact pin; ^ ~ ranges and latest are opt-in.

test-processor-dependencies.description: [test-processor-dependencies]: one dependency per key — a version string when the key is a catalog short name, a group:artifact[:version] string (versionless = platform-managed), "managed" on a catalog short name a platform BOM covers, or { group, name, version, features, ... }. A bare version is an exact pin; ^ ~ ranges and latest are opt-in.

platform-dependencies.description: [platform-dependencies]: one dependency per key — a version string when the key is a catalog short name, a group:artifact[:version] string (versionless = platform-managed), "managed" on a catalog short name a platform BOM covers, or { group, name, version, features, ... }. A bare version is an exact pin; ^ ~ ranges and latest are opt-in.

managed-dependencies.description: [managed-dependencies]: one managed version per key — a group:artifact:version string, a catalog short name with a version, or { group, name, version }. The entry pins the version a transitive dependency on the module resolves to, as Maven's inline dependencyManagement does; a version is required and the entry is not a classpath dependency of its own.

dev-dependencies.description: [dev-dependencies]: one dependency per key — a version string when the key is a catalog short name, a group:artifact[:version] string (versionless = platform-managed), "managed" on a catalog short name a platform BOM covers, or { group, name, version, features, ... }. A bare version is an exact pin; ^ ~ ranges and latest are opt-in.

test-dev-dependencies.description: [test-dev-dependencies]: one dependency per key — a version string when the key is a catalog short name, a group:artifact[:version] string (versionless = platform-managed), "managed" on a catalog short name a platform BOM covers, or { group, name, version, features, ... }. A bare version is an exact pin; ^ ~ ranges and latest are opt-in.

inherit.description: Cargo-style inheritance from the workspace root.
